gaps.sentence: Little ___ the chances of success be improved by patience.
gaps.explanation: Little will the chances be improved… — inversion with future.

gaps.sentence: To ___ did you address that complaint, exactly?
Enclosed ___ the contract a copy of the invoice.
gaps.explanation: 'Enclosed is the contract' — inversion after fronted participle.

gaps.sentence: Under no circumstances ___ this door be left unlocked.
gaps.explanation: Under no circumstances + must + subject + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: Barely ___ the survey published when the complaints arrived.
gaps.explanation: Barely had X happened when Y — like hardly… when.

gaps.sentence: Come ___ it may, the trial must proceed.
gaps.explanation: 'Come what may' — fixed inverted idiom = whatever happens.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ she apologise, she also paid for the damage.
gaps.explanation: Not only did she…, (but) she also… — inversion after not only.

gaps.sentence: So difficult ___ the exam that half the candidates failed.
gaps.explanation: So difficult was the exam that… — inversion for emphasis.
